scale: Each dimension is scored 0-5 (whole numbers). Total /100 = sum of (score / 5 x weight).
fairness: Accent, grammar, pronunciation and mixing Hindi with English never lower marks in any dimension except Communication, and in Communication only clarity and structure are judged, never accent or grammar. Recogniser (speech-to-text) mistakes are not the student's fault.

dimensions.name: Conceptual understanding
dimensions.looks_at: Answers to fundamentals and depth questions: are definitions and relationships correct and complete?

anchors.0: No relevant answer, or answers are fundamentally wrong.
anchors.1: Isolated keywords with little correct meaning; most questions unanswered.
anchors.2: Some correct ideas but major gaps or confusions on core concepts.
anchors.3: Core concepts mostly correct; some key points missing or imprecise.
anchors.4: Correct and fairly complete on nearly all questions, with minor gaps.
anchors.5: Precise, complete and correct; connects concepts to each other.

dimensions.name: Depth and reasoning
dimensions.looks_at: Follow-up ('why', 'what if') answers and the depth phase: does the student explain why, handle changed conditions, and reason about trade-offs?

anchors.0: No reasoning offered; cannot go beyond the first answer.
anchors.1: Restates facts when asked why; no trade-offs.
anchors.2: Some correct reasoning on one follow-up; struggles with 'what if'.
anchors.3: Explains why for most follow-ups; partial handling of changed conditions.
anchors.4: Clear causal reasoning and sensible trade-offs on several follow-ups.
anchors.5: Deep, well-justified reasoning; anticipates edge cases and trade-offs unprompted.

dimensions.name: Problem solving
dimensions.looks_at: The applied problem: does the student diagnose the cause, propose a workable fix, and check it?

anchors.0: No attempt at the applied problem.
anchors.1: Guesses without a method; does not identify the cause.
anchors.2: Identifies part of the problem; fix missing or unworkable.
anchors.3: Identifies the cause and a plausible fix, with gaps in reasoning or verification.
anchors.4: Systematic diagnosis and a workable fix with some justification.
anchors.5: Systematic, correct diagnosis; robust fix; considers trade-offs and how to verify.

dimensions.name: Practical / project knowledge
dimensions.looks_at: The project opener and practical details: concrete technologies, design decisions and the student's own contribution.

anchors.0: No project or practical knowledge described.
anchors.1: Vague project description; no concrete details or own role.
anchors.2: Some concrete details, unclear own contribution or design reasons.
anchors.3: Concrete project with own role; limited reasoning about design choices.
anchors.4: Concrete, specific project; explains own contribution and some design decisions.
anchors.5: Detailed, specific project knowledge; justifies design decisions and lessons learned.

dimensions.name: Communication
dimensions.looks_at: Clarity and structure of answers: stays on the question, organises points, uses examples. Not accent, grammar or language mix.

anchors.0: Answers cannot be followed or are entirely off-topic.
anchors.1: Mostly unclear or off-topic; ideas hard to follow.
anchors.2: Understandable but disorganised or frequently off-topic.
anchors.3: Generally clear and on-topic; limited structure or examples.
anchors.4: Clear, organised answers that stay on the question.
anchors.5: Very clear, well structured, concise answers with apt examples.
